title: Your Salary Expectations Answer: Hourly to Annual Pay with Tax and Super for 2026-27
description: Get your salary expectations answer: convert hourly rate to annual pay for 38-hour week, plus tax, Medicare, and super. Use Fair Work rates and ATO tax brackets.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay equals hourly rate × 38 × 52; the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week and then by 52. For full-time, we use 38 hours per week. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 annual gross. If you work part-time, use your actual weekly hours.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the national minimum wage, that's $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. The loading is added to your pay but does not include paid leave. Always enter your base rate without loading; the calculator adds it when you select casual.

faqs.q: How are tax and super calculated on the annual figure?
faqs.a: Tax uses the 2026-27 resident rates with the tax-free threshold: nil up to $18,200, then 15%, 30%, 37%, and 45% for higher brackets. Medicare levy is 2% (reductions apply for low income). Super is 12% of ordinary earnings paid on top by your employer, capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Salary Expectations Answer

When you're negotiating a job or comparing offers, you need a reliable **salary expectations answer** that accounts for the full picture: base hourly rate, hours per week, annual gross, tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. This guide walks you through the conversion using the standard 38-hour full-time week, the national minimum wage, award rates, and the 2026-27 tax scales.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The standard way to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week because that's the ordinary hours for full-time employment under the Fair Work system. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly. For example, a 20-hour week would use 20 instead of 38.

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage at **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, which equals **$1,004.90 per week**. This is the base rate for award/agreement-free adult employees.

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

Many employees are covered by an award, which sets higher minimum rates than the national minimum wage. You can find the correct rate for your classification using [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base rate. For the national minimum wage, that's **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). Always enter your base hourly rate without the loading; the calculator adds it when you select the casual option.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight**. This can help you budget between paydays. For a $30/hour full-time worker: $30 × 38 = $1,140 per week; $1,140 × 2 = $2,280 per fortnight.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross, the Australian Taxation Office applies the 2026-27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

On top of income tax, most residents pay the **Medicare levy** of 2% of taxable income. There are reductions for low-income earners (using 2025-26 thresholds as 2026-27 reductions were not confirmed). For a single person, the full Medicare levy applies once income exceeds about $27,000.

Example: For an annual gross of $80,000 (say $40.50/hour × 38 × 52), the tax would be approximately $4,020 + 0.30 × ($80,000 - $45,000) = $4,020 + $10,500 = $14,520. Medicare levy adds 2% = $1,600. Total tax and Medicare = $16,120, leaving about $63,880 after tax.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee of **12%** of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your gross pay; it's an additional contribution to your super fund. The maximum earnings base for super is **$270,830** per year. So if your annual gross is above that, super is capped at $32,499.60 (12% of $270,830).

For a worker on $80,000, the employer pays an extra $9,600 into super, making total employment cost $89,600. Your take-home pay is after tax, not after super.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then calculates weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross, estimates tax and Medicare, and shows super on top. Remember: the annual figure is an estimate assuming the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

Your salary expectations answer depends on the correct hourly rate for your award or agreement, the hours you work, and the tax and super rules. Always check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [pay guides](/blog) for your industry. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 for full-time, then apply tax and Medicare to get your net annual income, and remember super is extra. For a broader perspective, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, or about $108,352 annually. That's a benchmark, but your rate depends on your specific job.
